winning_case.argument: Not yet: he's improved, but average doesn't carry a franchise.

royce.claim: Not yet: a franchise quarterback has won when it mattered, and Young's record and one playoff start haven't answered that.
supports: Record: 3-4 this season and 0-1 in the playoffs (F4, F5)
Draft pedigree raises the bar: first overall pick (F12)
Turn: Deacon's rank is middle of the pack, which is not a franchise label (F10)
royce.answer: Concedes the offense scores, then says a franchise quarterback is the reason, not a passenger, and the numbers show a middle-of-the-pack player.

deacon.claim: Not yet: he is a league-average starter on efficiency, up from last year but not elite.
supports: EPA per dropback +0.05, 17th of 35, vs -0.01 and 29th of 38 last season (F10, F13)
Completion 58.7% and 5 picks in 7 games (F9, F8)
deacon.answer: Grants the improvement is real and says better than last year is not the same as franchise.

lonnie.claim: Yes, he's the guy you build around: the offense is working with him and the improvement is real, so you commit.
supports: Role and fit: deep-throwing style, low aggressiveness into tight coverage, and the team is 9th in scoring and 12th in offensive EPA (F15, F16)
Availability: 7 of 7 games this season, 16 of 17 and 14 of 17 before (F3)
Production: 1,921 yards, 13 TD, 5 INT (F6, F7, F8)
lonnie.answer: Concedes the record is 3-4, then says the franchise label is about whether you can build around him, and the point is he's trending up.

beats: Opening positions: Lonnie says yes, Deacon says average so no
Main clash: last season to this season. Is the improvement real or a small bump?
Trap: Royce gets Lonnie to commit to the offense as the evidence, then points to the 3-4 record and the playoff loss
Decisive: Deacon corners the yes case with the rank, and Lonnie has to say what would flip him

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: You're on the Sideline. Go ahead, Ray from Charlotte.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Everybody wants to hand Bryce Young the keys to Carolina. I don't buy it. Convince me he's a franchise quarterback.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: I'll convince you. Yes. Look at how they use him. To my eye he's a guy who fits what they want, and the offense backs it up: ninth in the league in scoring.

stat.label: Carolina Panthers · points scored per game
stat.definition: Points the team scored per regular-season game.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Ninth in scoring is a team stat, Lonnie. Look at him. EPA per dropback, that's the points each pass play adds to what the offense should score. He's at plus 0.05, seventeenth of thirty-five. That's the middle of the pack. Middle isn't a franchise.

stat.label: Bryce Young · EPA per dropback
stat.definition: Expected points added per dropback: how much each pass attempt, sack, or scramble raised or lowered the points his team should expect on that drive.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: And a franchise quarterback was the first pick in the draft, Lonnie. That's the price they paid. At that price you don't get to be pretty good. Three and four this season, and his one playoff start was a loss.

stat.label: Bryce Young · record as a starting QB
stat.definition: Regular-season wins and losses in games he started at quarterback.
stat.source: nflverse, checked against Sleeper (games started, every season)

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Hold on, Royce, I'll give him something. Last year he was minus 0.01, twenty-ninth of thirty-eight. So he's up. Real up. I'm not arguing that.

stat.label: Bryce Young · EPA per dropback
stat.definition: Expected points added per dropback: how much each pass attempt, sack, or scramble raised or lowered the points his team should expect on that drive.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Thank you. So that's the trend, and a franchise quarterback is a trend plus a roster you can build on. Last season his yards per dropback, adjusted for touchdowns and picks, was 5.49. This year it's 6.23. Canales is the coach today, and he's getting better.

stat.label: Bryce Young · adjusted net yards per attempt (ANY/A)
stat.definition: Passing yards per dropback, with touchdowns worth 20 extra yards, interceptions costing 45, and sack yardage taken off.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Seven games, Lonnie. I'm the one who says that, and I'm saying it. Seven games of improvement is a good start. It isn't a verdict.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Here's what I'd ask. Lonnie, you want to build around him. What's the evidence he's the reason it works? Not the team. Him.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Fair. He's played every game this season, and 16 of 17 and 14 of 17 before that. Thirteen touchdowns to five picks. You can build around a guy who's on the field.

stat.value: 2023: 16 of 17; 2024: 14 of 17; 2025: 16 of 17; 2026: 7 of 7 so far, through Week 8. In his last 3 full seasons he played every game in 0 and missed a quarter or more of his team's games in 0
stat.label: Bryce Young · games played by season
stat.definition: Games he played each regular season, out of his team's games. Missing games can be injury, rest, suspension, or not being on a roster yet; this doesn't say which.
stat.asOf: last 5 full seasons and this one · today

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Available. Okay. Available isn't franchise. To my eye he's a steady hand, a guy who takes what's there. That's a good starter. Franchise means you win games because of him, and the record's 3-4.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Five picks in seven games, 58.7 percent completions. That's not the efficient guy you'd bank on.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Five picks in seven games doesn't tell me he's a gunslinger, that's my read. Anyway, you're both grading him on a record. The question is whether you commit.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Then answer this. If he goes to the playoffs again and loses, are you still building around him?

stat.label: Bryce Young · playoff record as a starting QB
stat.definition: Playoff wins and losses in games he started at quarterback.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Yes. One playoff start doesn't change a plan. If his efficiency slides back to where it was last year, I change my answer.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: There it is. So you're already saying the number could flip you. That's a not-yet, Lonnie, not a yes.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: It's a yes with a condition. Everybody's is.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: Final answers. One sentence each. Deacon.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Not yet: he's improved, but average doesn't carry a franchise.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Not yet: a franchise quarterback wins the games that matter, and he hasn't.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Yes: he fits the offense, he's on the field, and he's trending the right way.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: On the scorecard, tonight goes to Deacon. His case was that the offense's ninth-place scoring is a team number, and that on his own plays Young sits in the middle of the pack, seventeenth of thirty-five.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: That's the board. Thanks for the call, Ray.
